title: Make the tool usable
subtitle: Give another person a clear route to a useful local report.
courseLabel: Harness in practice · Tutorial 5 of 6 · Deliver
coursePath: Turn an idea into a useful result
Decide whether to trust the report
Make it work for your needs

sections.title: Make the useful result easy to obtain
sections.intro: A report is more useful when another person can generate it from the instructions, recognize its output and recover from a common problem.
sections.html:
Click Open formatted report to see the result the local instructions lead toward.

This lesson uses the supplied current reporting program. You will download it, find the correct folder, generate HTML and check the result. The Python program needs no model call.

Delivery means a usable local package and instructions. Publication, deployment and sharing another person's activity data are separate tasks.

Read the course setup instructions. Use synthetic data throughout.
presenterNotes: Let the learner say who would use the report and what they need to do with it.
Opening a supplied report is not a new AI build.

sections.title: Find the folder the commands need
sections.intro: The command is short. Selecting the correct extracted folder is the prerequisite that makes it work.
sections.html:
1. Click Download checked example ZIP.
  2. Extract the ZIP to a new practice folder. Keep any previous extraction and reports intact.
  3. Find the extracted folder containing report.py and data/activity.csv. The ZIP stores those paths at its root; your extraction tool may wrap them in another folder.
  4. Ask your assistant for the exact cd command to enter that folder. On Mac, you can type cd followed by a space in Terminal, drag that folder from Finder into Terminal and press Return.

Use an existing Python 3.12 environment as described in Runnable reference instructions. The optional test command additionally needs pytest.

Folder check: can you locate the script and the CSV named by the next command? If either is absent, correct the folder before running it.
presenterNotes: Allow time for extracting and selecting the folder. Do not assume the learner knows the current working directory.
Use the actual download link. Do not invent a browser extraction control or promise the same folder name across extraction tools.

sections.title: Create a report you can open
sections.intro: From the extracted example folder, run the program on the supplied synthetic CSV and choose a new output filename.
sections.html:
Read the command before running it. It reads data/activity.csv and creates activity-report.html in the current folder. It does not call a model.

Expected result: Saved report to activity-report.html. Ask your assistant to open that file in your browser, or open it yourself.

If the destination already exists, the program refuses it with Output error: the output path already exists; choose a new path. Keep the existing file and choose an unused name, such as activity-report-second.html, in the --output argument. Open the same filename you selected.

Invalid input is reported before a report is written. If the command reports an input or output error, retain the message and inspect the named path before trying again.
presenterNotes: This argv is verified against the bundled parser and README: one CSV path, --format html and --output path.
A refusal to overwrite is expected behavior, not a reason to delete the previous result. No fresh execution is claimed by the lesson text.

sections.title: Connect the report to its source
sections.intro: A successful file write tells you a file was created. Check that it contains the result you intended.
sections.html:
1. Confirm the report covers 19–21 October 2026, with 6 entries and 270 minutes or 4 hours 30 minutes.
  2. Compare the project totals: Orion 180 and Lumen 90.
  3. Compare the category totals: Development 150, Documentation 75 and Testing 45.
  4. Read one row in data/activity.csv and explain where it contributes to the totals.

The report is a standalone HTML file with a print layout. Use your browser's print command if you want a paper or PDF copy, then inspect the preview before saving or printing.

Optional: inspect the baseline text output

Read this command before running it. It prints the same grouping as plain text and creates no report file.

Compare the output with Expected text report.

Optional: run the supplied checks

If your selected Python 3.12 environment already includes pytest, follow the test command and limits in Runnable reference instructions. Read the current software-check record, then record your own actual output with its selected source and environment.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to find their generated file rather than reopening the supplied expected file by mistake.
Software checks, the learner’s execution and a print preview are distinct evidence.

sections.title: Change a copy and predict the result
sections.intro: Practice changing input without losing the original six-row fixture or a previous report.
sections.html:
1. Copy data/activity.csv to a new file named data/activity-practice.csv.
  2. In that copy only, change Lumen's Documentation entry from 30 to 45 minutes. Keep the original fixture unchanged.
  3. Predict the effect before running: 6 entries and 285 minutes; Orion 180; Lumen 105; Development 150; Documentation 90; Testing 45.
  4. Choose an unused output filename and run the practice command. Compare its actual result with your prediction.

Read the command before running it. It selects the practice copy and a different output path.

The expected totals above are calculated from the proposed input change. They are not a recorded execution result. If your output differs, inspect the edited row and command rather than changing the expected answer to match.
presenterNotes: This variation is optional and should use a separate input and output. Preserve the supplied fixture and any earlier learner result.
The test suite uses the original fixture, so changing a practice copy should not rewrite its baseline.

sections.title: Give the next person one clear route
sections.intro: Write instructions around the actual folder, command, expected result and common refusal.
sections.html:
Filled local handoff

Purpose: summarize synthetic project activity by project and category.

Prerequisite: extract the checked example and use an existing Python 3.12 environment. Run commands from the folder containing report.py and data/activity.csv.

Run: use the HTML report command in this lesson and a new output path.

Expected sample: 6 entries, 270 minutes, Orion 180 and Lumen 90.

Recovery: an existing destination is preserved; select another filename. Keep an error message with the inputs that caused it.

Evidence: link the CSV, expected report and current software-check record. Record a new reader's actual outcome separately.

Limit: this is a local synthetic-data reference. No deployment, real-data sharing or cross-platform acceptance is claimed.

This optional note stays in local browser storage when available. It does not publish or send the handoff.
presenterNotes: Ask whether a reader can obtain every input and distinguish expected from observed output.
Record help needed when someone tries the instructions; do not infer a measured learning outcome from completion.

sections.title: Know what is ready and what still needs checking
sections.intro: You can now explain how to obtain the report and how to preserve a previous result.
sections.html:
Explain the handoff in your own words: where to start, which file is produced, how to check one number and what happens when the destination already exists.

A local file that you can open is useful progress. Another person's successful walkthrough, their help needed and any platform or printer observations are additional evidence to collect rather than assume.

Current version and verification limits

This lesson targets Harness 1.7.0 preparation at source 5159e7a79fbdb84d2982937716043b142534e6e9. Version 1.7.0 is unpublished. Follow the course setup instructions for the selected runtime.

Read the current software-check record for the exact checked files, commands, environment and results. These local checks make no model call. They do not establish every input, platform, model outcome or learner experience.

Next: Open Tutorial 6: Make it work for your needs to prepare one bounded change.
presenterNotes: The optional check never locks the next lesson.
Invite the learner to explain a recovery decision with less prompting.

check.question: A previous activity-report.html already exists. What is the supported next action?

options.text: Keep it and use an unused --output filename, then open that same new file.
options.feedback: Correct. The reporting tool creates a new file and refuses to overwrite an existing destination.

options.text: Run the same command again and expect it to replace the old report.
options.feedback: The existing-file refusal is intentional. Select a new output path and preserve the previous result.
